diagram_candidates.claim: Every subset T gives a rectangular box C_T; the Davis cellulation has 8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 square faces and one 3-cell; its boundary is S^2, whose dual Coxeter complex is an octahedron with 6 vertices and 8 triangles.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The item explicitly contrasts the cubical boundary sphere with its dual octahedral Coxeter cellulation, and states cell counts and chamber incidence that a compact picture can make checkable.
diagram_candidates.diagram_to_draw_or_check: Draw a cube with eight sign-vector vertices, twelve edges and six square faces, then its dual octahedron with six vertices and eight triangular chambers. Identify a cube vertex with a Coxeter chamber (one sign choice in each of three opposite coordinate pairs); identify cube faces with parabolic cosets and show duality reverses incidence. Use labels consistently so the two cellulations are visibly different.
diagram_candidates.confidence: warranted, mathematical maps directly supported by source; the exact diagram layout is editorial.

local_image_evidence.observation: Tiles show the source claim for the box, its 8/12/6/1 cell counts, the octahedral dual and the two distinct boundary cellulations; no diagram is rendered.

diagram_candidates.claim: The heap for u=s1s3 is a two-element antichain and [1,u]_R has four elements; the heap for w=s1s3s2 is V-shaped with 1<3 and 2<3 and [1,w]_R has five elements.
diagram_candidates.kind: two heap posets with order-ideal lattices and weak-order interval maps
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The example’s point is the explicit order isomorphism from weak intervals to order ideals; paired Hasse diagrams would show the two mappings and distributive lattice operations at a glance.
diagram_candidates.diagram_to_draw_or_check: For the antichain, draw s1 and s3 incomparable and the Boolean square J(P_u), labeling 1↔∅, s1↔{1}, s3↔{2}, u↔{1,2}. For the V heap, draw 1<3 and 2<3 and its five-ideal lattice, labeling 1↔∅, s1↔{1}, s3↔{2}, s1s3↔{1,2}, w↔{1,2,3}. Arrows must increase both weak-order length and ideal inclusion.
diagram_candidates.confidence: warranted; all vertices, relations, and maps are explicitly stated in the source.

local_image_evidence.observation: Tile 01 explicitly states the antichain and V-shaped heap and the 4/5 element intervals; tile 03 shows their ideal-set verification. No Hasse diagram is rendered.

diagram_candidates.claim: Five root lines cut S^1 into ten spherical chambers; the Coxeter complex is a ten-edge, ten-vertex circle; each chamber subtends π/5, with the two vertex types distinguished by the rank-one parabolics.
diagram_candidates.kind: rank-two spherical chamber and Coxeter-complex illustration
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The item gives a concrete geometric model whose chamber count, adjacency, vertex stabilizers, and angle can be cross-checked visually.
diagram_candidates.diagram_to_draw_or_check: Draw five distinct lines through the origin, their ten intersection points with S^1, and label the ten intervening arcs as chambers. Mark the fundamental arc C∩S^1 with angle π/5; distinguish the two alternating vertex orbits by W_{ {s} } and W_{ {t} }. Show adjacent chambers sharing one endpoint. Avoid assigning an oriented word sequence around the circle unless the group-action convention is explicitly verified.
diagram_candidates.confidence: warranted; count and angle are confirmed by source, while a particular oriented labeling is intentionally left open.

local_image_evidence.observation: Tile 01 states five root lines and ten chambers; tiles 04–05 verify chamber/vertex incidence and the π/5 angle. No spherical Coxeter complex diagram is rendered.

diagram_candidates.claim: The 64 subwords of a fixed reduced expression for w0=4321 realize all 24 elements; deleting positions 1,4,6 gives the three covers 4312,4231,3421 while other single deletions give lower-rank values.
diagram_candidates.kind: small Bruhat cover diagram around the longest element
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: A small interval/cover view could clarify which reflection deletions are covers and which are strictly lower despite being single-letter deletions.
diagram_candidates.diagram_to_draw_or_check: Draw only the local star below w0=4321: immediate lower covers 4312, 4231, 3421 at rank 5. If showing noncovers, place 4123 and 2341 at rank 3 and 1324 at rank 1 without connecting them as covers of w0. Do not attempt to depict the full 24-element Bruhat interval in this local diagram.
diagram_candidates.confidence: optional editorial aid; the finite computation is already clear in the text.

local_image_evidence.observation: Tile 01 lists the three rank-five covers alongside lower-rank deletion values; tile 03 verifies the cover criterion. No Bruhat cover diagram is rendered.

diagram_candidates.claim: The heap of s1s2s1 is the chain 1<2<3, its labels alternate and trigger the forbidden length-three braid, while s1s2s1 and s2s1s2 lie in different commutation classes.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: A three-node labeled chain beside the two braid-related words can make the exact forbidden convex alternating chain visible.
diagram_candidates.diagram_to_draw_or_check: Draw the chain 1<2<3 with labels s1,s2,s1; separately list the two reduced words s1s2s1 and s2s1s2 as distinct commutation classes, joined only by the length-three braid relation. Do not depict them as heap-equivalent.
diagram_candidates.confidence: optional editorial aid; claims are already explicit.

local_image_evidence.observation: Tile 01 states the labeled chain and braid-related words in distinct commutation classes; tile 02 verifies the heap relations. No heap diagram is rendered.
